title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. Grothendieck is building elementary definitions for a theory of 'déploiement' of stratified spaces via conic and cylindrical neighbourhoods. The previous page set up the following data:
- Y is a closed subset of X, and T is a conic neighbourhood of Y. This means an action of the multiplicative interval I = [0,1] on T, a 'boundary' Ṫ = T_1, and T obtained as the image of I×Ṫ union Y.
- A subset T' ⊂ T is called conic if it is stable under the action of λ and is itself a conic neighbourhood. 'Strict' means T'∩Y = 0·Ṫ'.
- T is compatible with a closed set X' ⊂ X if X'∩T is conic in T.
- T is strictly compatible with X' if, in addition, T is strict and the boundary Ṫ has a cylindrical neighbourhood in X* = X \ T° that is compatible with X'* = X'∩X*.

This page.

1. It finishes that definition explicitly. There must be a neighbourhood E of Ṫ in X* and a homeomorphism E ≅ Ṫ×[0,1]. Under it, the inclusion Ṫ ↪ E becomes t ↦ (t,0), so E is a collar of Ṫ in the 'exterior' X*. Moreover X'∩E must correspond to X'_0×[0,1] with X'_0 closed in Ṫ (necessarily X'_0 = X'∩Ṫ).

2. It then abstracts this to an arbitrary closed subset B of a space X. A cylindrical neighbourhood of B in X is a collar E ≅ B×[0,1] with B = B×{0}; this implicitly forces B to behave like a boundary of X. A closed X' is called compatible with E, renamed 'transversal' to E (both in the text and in the margin), if X'∩E ≅ B'×[0,1], where necessarily B' = X'∩B.

3. Grothendieck warns that this cylindrical transversality is NOT a special case of conic compatibility. A crossed-out formula shows what the conic analogue would be: X'∩T ≅ B'×[0,1] ∪ B×{0}. That is, in the conic case X' may contain the whole core, whereas transversality to a collar is a product condition along the whole collar. A margin note seems to say the condition is on X' and not just on B∩X'.

4. Finally, the definition is extended to a family (X_i)_{i∈I} of closed parts. The next page then defines 'B compatible with a family (X_i)' as the existence of a collar simultaneously transversal to all X_i. It reformulates strict compatibility of conic neighbourhoods in these terms, which leads to quasi-regular and regular conic neighbourhoods (Ṫ → Y, and Ṫ_i → Y, locally trivial fibrations).

Purpose. These are axioms for 'tame' stratified spaces in which every stratum has a conic (mapping-cylinder) neighbourhood whose boundary is collared compatibly with the other strata. This is the groundwork for 'déployer' (unfold/resolve) a stratified space into a manifold-with-corners-like object.
errors: 'B une partie fermée stricte' (reading uncertain). For a collar E ≅ B×[0,1] that is a neighbourhood of B to exist, B must be boundary-like in X. This is an implicit hypothesis, not a stated one.
In the conic-case formula crossed out at the bottom, the symbol is written as Ṫ, although by the logic it should be T, or X'∩T. Grothendieck crossed the line out anyway.
No genuine mathematical error. The definitions are consistent; for instance B' = X'∩B is indeed forced.

ideas.what: Strict compatibility of a conic neighbourhood T of Y with a closed set X': the boundary Ṫ admits a collar in X \ T° in which X' is a product X'_0×[0,1]
ideas.modern_name: Stratified collar / control data compatible with strata; mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods with collared boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969) and Mather (1970) control data; Siebenmann (1972) locally conelike stratified sets; Quinn (1988) and Hughes for homotopically stratified sets
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6, speaks informally of dévissage of stratified structures and tubular neighbourhoods, not of these precise definitions

ideas.what: Cylindrical neighbourhood (collar) of a closed subset B and transversality of a closed X' to it (X'∩E = (X'∩B)×[0,1])
ideas.modern_name: Collar of a boundary; subspace transverse to a collar (product structure)

ideas.what: Observation that cylindrical transversality is not a special case of conic compatibility (the conic analogue would be B'×[0,1] ∪ B×{0})
ideas.modern_name: Difference between cone-compatibility and product/collar compatibility

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful but routine foundational definitions (collars and conic neighbourhoods compatible with closed subsets) that parallel Thom–Mather–Siebenmann notions. They are of archival interest as part of Grothendieck's 'déploiement' programme, but contain no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: The left-margin diagonal note near the definition reads roughly '(compatibilité →) transversalité !', recording the change of terminology.
'Soit B une partie fermée stricte' is uncertain; the word may be 'bord' or another word, so read it as 'partie [fermée?] stricte'.
In the crossed-out final lines, the interlinear insertion reads roughly 'plus exigeante, qui correspond au cas où on demandait T'∩Y = 0·Ṫ'', followed by the crossed formula 'X'∩Ṫ ≃ B'×[0,1] ∪ B×{0}'.
The left lower margin note, hard to read, seems to say something like 'cela n'impose [aucune?] condition sur B∩X' ... X'', i.e. a remark about what is constrained (B∩X' versus X').
The word above X' in 'une partie X' de X' is 'fermée' (inserted).
